page: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a 320 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 937 GB NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 placing it in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded tasks perform well, as evidenced by strong results in gzip compression (34.34 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.1 GB/sec). However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance (4390.87) and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (28.17 GB/sec) are categorized as weak, reflecting the physical core count of two. Memory read bandwidth is also weak, measuring 343.61 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 33.73 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though write bandwidth for large blocks is average at 35.58 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i7i.xlarge offers a high density of local NVMe SSD storage and DDR5 memory relative to its 4 vCPUs, making it a specialized option for workloads that require fast local storage access without demanding massive multi-core compute scaling. It is suitable for database operations, caching layers, and text processing tasks. However, it is less optimal for highly parallelized multi-threaded applications, software compilation, or memory-bandwidth-intensive workloads due to its lower multi-core and read bandwidth performance.
